scope: Williamson County, TX (Round Rock, Georgetown, Cedar Park, Leander, Hutto, Taylor, Pflugerville part) - food, housing, utilities, cash assistance, transportation, plus local health/workforce/legal providers

records.name: The Serving Center Food Pantry
records.description_en: A food pantry that gives groceries to people who need them. It also runs Fresh Food For Families produce days and a senior food program.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in Round Rock and southern Williamson County who need food. You must apply online and get a food voucher before you visit.
records.how_to_apply: Apply online on the Serving Center website to get a food voucher, then visit the pantry. If you do not have a computer, call to set up a time to meet with staff.
records.hours: Food Pantry: Mon-Fri 10am-4pm (final check-in 3:30pm), Sat 9am-1pm. Fresh Food For Families: 1st, 3rd & 5th Thursday 7:30-9:30am. H.O.P.E. (elderly): 2nd Friday 9am-1pm.
records.notes: Site says food assistance may be given without photo ID. Email: hello@rrasc.org.

records.name: Emergency Financial Assistance (Rent, Utilities, Prescriptions, Transportation)
records.description_en: Helps with rent, utility bills, prescriptions, payday loan help, transportation, temporary lodging, and clothing and furniture vouchers.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in Round Rock and southern Williamson County facing a money crisis. Call or apply online to learn if you qualify.
records.how_to_apply: Apply online on the Serving Center website or call to make an appointment. Pick up vouchers or checks during packet pick-up hours.
records.notes: Specific eligibility and documents not posted; call to confirm.

records.name: Amazon Home Delivery Program
records.description_en: Delivers food to the homes of older adults, people with disabilities, and veterans or active military.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For adults 60 and older, people with disabilities, veterans, and active military who live in Williamson County (except zip codes 76530 and 76577).
records.how_to_apply: Call the Serving Center to enroll.
records.notes: Eligible groups: 60+, disabled, veterans, active military (any one qualifies).

records.name: The Caring Place Food Pantry
records.description_en: A food pantry in Georgetown that gives a food order to families in need. It also offers free laundry days.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people living in Georgetown, Andice, Bartlett, Florence, Granger, Jarrell, Jonah, Schwertner, Walburg, Weir, or the part of Hutto in Georgetown ISD.

eligibility_rules.residency_required: Georgetown and north Williamson County communities listed

records.how_to_apply: Walk in during pantry hours. First-time visitors may need to get a 'Caring Card' at 2001 Railroad Ave. first.
records.notes: Loads of Caring free laundry: 2nd Tuesday and last Thursday of each month, 4-8pm.

records.name: The Caring Place Financial Assistance
records.description_en: Helps families in crisis with rent or mortgage, utility bills, transportation, emergency medical needs, and case management.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people living in Georgetown and nearby north Williamson County communities who are in a money crisis.

eligibility_rules.residency_required: Georgetown and north Williamson County communities listed

records.how_to_apply: Come to Programs & Services at 2001 Railroad Ave. Check in by 3 PM if you are asking for financial help.
records.hours: Mon-Fri 9am-4pm (check in by 3pm for financial assistance)
records.notes: Also administers Georgetown Utility Systems' Good Neighbor Fund. Service area: Georgetown, Andice, Bartlett, Florence, Granger, Jarrell, Jonah, Schwertner, Walburg, Weir, and Hutto within GISD.

records.name: HCCM Food Pantry and Community Cupboard
records.description_en: A food pantry with shelf-stable food, fresh food, and personal care items for families in the Leander and Cedar Park area.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in crisis or living in poverty in southwest Williamson County and nearby northwest Travis County. Call to check if your area is served.
records.how_to_apply: Call HCCM or visit during open hours.
records.hours: Mon-Fri 9am-12pm and 1pm-3pm; Thursday extended until 7pm. Community Cupboard closes 10 minutes before facility closing.
records.notes: Serves Cedar Park and Leander area. Thrift store at 1501 Leander Drive, Bldg. C, Unit 3, Leander, (512) 334-6464.

records.name: HCCM Other Assistance (Rent and Utility Help)
records.description_en: Gives help with rent, utility bills, and other urgent needs for families in the Leander and Cedar Park area.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in crisis in southwest Williamson County and nearby northwest Travis County. Call to see if you qualify.
records.how_to_apply: Call HCCM to ask about rent or utility help.
records.notes: Eligibility and required documents are not posted on the site.

records.name: Comprehensive Energy Assistance Program (CEAP)
records.description_en: Helps low-income households pay electric and heating bills and teaches ways to save energy.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income households living in Williamson or Burnet County. Income must be within the federal poverty guidelines OWBC posts.
documents_needed: Proof of income for the last 30 days for everyone 18 and older (pay stubs, unemployment, SNAP letter, child support, or award letters)
Photo ID and proof of citizenship or legal residence for at least one household member (SAVE form)
Signed information release if you have Atmos or City of Austin utilities
records.how_to_apply: Download the application (English or Spanish) from the OWBC website, fill out every section, and send it in with your documents. Processing can take up to 90 days after your application is complete.
records.notes: Email utilities@owbc-tx.org. TDHCA Help for Texans lists phone (512) 255-2202 for this CEAP provider; OWBC's own site lists (512) 763-1400. OWBC also distributes PEC Member Assistance funds in Williamson County.

records.name: Meals on Wheels and Congregate Meals
records.description_en: Brings hot meals to the homes of people who cannot cook for themselves because of age, illness, or disability. Also serves noon meals at senior centers on weekdays.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For older adults and people who are homebound because of illness or disability in Williamson and Burnet counties.
records.how_to_apply: Call OWBC to ask about home-delivered meals or senior center meals.
records.notes: Email information@owbc-tx.org. Exact age limits and cost not posted.

records.name: Head Start
records.description_en: Free early learning program for young children that also helps families work toward their goals.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For young children from income-eligible families in Williamson and Burnet counties. Call to check age and income rules.
records.how_to_apply: Call or email OWBC to ask about enrolling your child.
records.notes: Email information@owbc-tx.org. Enrolled 495 children in 2024 per OWBC.

records.name: Hutto Resource Center Food Pantry
records.description_en: Gives out food, meat, fresh produce, diapers, and hygiene and household items through a drive-thru and a weekly pop-up.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For anyone living in Hutto or the Hutto ISD attendance zone. There are no income requirements.

eligibility_rules.residency_required: Hutto or Hutto ISD attendance zone

records.how_to_apply: Call before your first visit or use the QR code on the website to register. You will get a barcode by email to show at your first distribution.
records.hours: Wednesday Pop-Up: every Wednesday 2:00-3:30pm. Saturday Drive-Thru: 1st, 3rd and 5th Saturday 9:00am-12:00pm.
records.notes: Some directories list 512-688-0612; the official site lists 512-688-0162.

records.name: Shepherd's Heart Food Pantry
records.organization: Shepherd's Heart Food Pantry & Community Ministries
records.description_en: A drive-up food pantry in Taylor that gives shelf-stable food, dairy, produce, bread, and sometimes meat.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in and around Taylor who need food.
records.how_to_apply: Drive up during pantry hours. Volunteers will load groceries into your trunk.
records.notes: Volunteer-run. Thrift shop open Tue, Wed, Thu & Sat 9am-3pm when volunteers are available.

records.name: Central Texas Food Bank - Find Food Now
records.description_en: The regional food bank that supplies local pantries and runs mobile food pantries. Its Find Food Now tool shows food sites near your ZIP code.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For anyone in its 21-county area, including Williamson County, who needs food.
records.how_to_apply: Use the Find Food Now tool on the website and enter your ZIP code, or call the food bank. It also helps people apply for SNAP.
records.notes: SNAP application help: https://www.centraltexasfoodbank.org/get-help/snap

records.name: Williamson County WIC
records.organization: Williamson County and Cities Health District (WCCHD)
records.description_en: Gives healthy food, nutrition advice from a dietitian, and breastfeeding support to moms and young kids.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For pregnant women, breastfeeding women, and families with children under 5 who meet income rules. Having a job or private insurance does not disqualify you.
documents_needed: Proof of household income (pay stubs, tax return, etc.) or proof of Medicaid, TANF, or SNAP
Proof of address (utility bill or rent receipt; no PO Boxes)
records.how_to_apply: Call the WIC clinic nearest you to make an appointment.
records.notes: Clinics: Round Rock, 355 Texas Ave, (512) 248-3254; Cedar Park, 350 Discovery Blvd #102, (512) 260-4241; Georgetown, Carver Center for Families, 1200 W 17th St, (512) 943-3680; Taylor, 115 W 6th St, (512) 238-2109; Liberty Hill (appointment only), 155 Hillcrest Lane, (512) 943-3680. Main office (512) 943-3600. People on Medicaid, TANF, or SNAP automatically meet income rules.

records.name: WilCo Care (County Indigent Health Care Program)
records.organization: Williamson County and Cities Health District (WCCHD)
records.description_en: Pays for doctor visits, tests, hospital care, up to 3 prescriptions a month, and counseling for very low-income adults who cannot get Medicaid.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For Williamson County adults 18 and older with income below 21% of the federal poverty level who are not eligible for Medicaid and have a valid Social Security card.
records.how_to_apply: Call the Healthcare Helpline or email pess@wilcotx.gov to apply.
records.notes: Hospital coverage max 30 days or $30,000 per year; program cap $30,000 per program year. Countable resources must meet Health & Safety Code 61.008.

records.name: Benefits Enrollment Center
records.organization: Williamson County and Cities Health District (WCCHD)
records.description_en: Helps older adults and people with disabilities apply for Medicare Extra Help, Medicare Savings Programs, Medicaid, and SNAP food benefits.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For adults 65 and older and people with disabilities.
records.how_to_apply: Call the WCCHD Healthcare Helpline to get help applying.
records.notes: The source page lists the Healthcare Helpline for WCCHD health resources; confirm the direct number for the Benefits Enrollment Center when calling.

records.name: Cancer Screening Initiative
records.organization: Williamson County and Cities Health District (WCCHD)
records.description_en: Gives breast, colorectal, and prostate cancer screening and treatment support to uninsured people.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For uninsured people with income at or below 250% of the federal poverty level. Age rules depend on the screening.
records.how_to_apply: Call the WCCHD Healthcare Helpline to ask about screening.
records.notes: Phone is the WCCHD Healthcare Helpline listed on the same page; confirm routing.

records.name: Bluebonnet Trails Community Services (Local Mental Health Authority)
records.description_en: Provides mental health counseling, medicine management, substance use counseling, disability (IDD) services, and 24/7 crisis help.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in 8 Central Texas counties, including Williamson County. Anyone in a mental health crisis can call the crisis line any time.
records.how_to_apply: Call the appointments line to start services. In a crisis, call the 24/7 crisis line.
records.notes: 24/7 Crisis Line: 1-800-841-1255. Mobile Crisis Outreach Team available 24/7. Diversion Center in Georgetown offers 23-48 hour observation. Youth and adult crisis respite in Round Rock. Also has locations in Cedar Park, Liberty Hill, and Taylor.

records.name: Hope Alliance Crisis Center and Emergency Shelter
records.description_en: Gives a 24-hour hotline, safe emergency shelter, counseling, case management, and legal advocacy for people hurt by family or sexual violence.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For survivors of domestic or sexual violence of any gender in Williamson County. Being homeless alone does not qualify you for this shelter.
records.how_to_apply: Call the 24-hour hotline or use HOPELine chat on the website. Hotline staff do shelter screening.
records.hours: Hotline 24 hours a day, 365 days a year
records.notes: Shelter location is confidential. Average shelter stay about 30 days. No text or email contact for confidentiality reasons.

records.name: Workforce Solutions of Williamson (Round Rock Office)
records.description_en: Local job center that helps people find work, get training, and apply for child care help.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For job seekers in the Rural Capital Area, including Williamson County.
records.how_to_apply: Visit or call the Round Rock office.
records.address: 575 Round Rock West Drive, Building H, Suite 240
records.notes: Office hours not posted on the locations page.

records.name: Workforce Solutions of Taylor
records.description_en: Local job center in Taylor that helps people find jobs and training.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For job seekers in the Rural Capital Area, including Williamson County.
records.how_to_apply: Visit or call the Taylor office.

records.name: Child Care Services Scholarship Program
records.description_en: Helps pay for child care so parents can work, go to school, or attend training.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For families living in Williamson or other Rural Capital counties who meet income limits. Single parents must work or study at least 25 hours a week; two-parent homes at least 50 hours combined.

eligibility_rules.residency_required: Resident of Bastrop, Blanco, Burnet, Caldwell, Fayette, Hays, Lee, Llano, or Williamson County

records.how_to_apply: Apply online through the Texas Workforce Commission child care portal. There is often a waitlist; some families (such as SNAP/TANF, homeless, veterans' children) get priority.
records.cost: Parent share of cost may apply
records.notes: Email rcachildcareservices@ruralcapital.net; fax 855-584-7332. Income limits in the posted 'Child Care Services Income Eligibility Limits (Effective October 1, 2025)' PDF.

records.name: Lone Star Circle of Care Community Health Centers
records.description_en: Community health centers that offer family medicine, pediatrics, women's care, dental, vision, behavioral health, and pharmacy. Fees can be on a sliding scale.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For anyone, including people with no insurance. Sliding fees are based on household income.
records.how_to_apply: Call the appointment line or self-schedule online.
records.notes: Williamson County sites: Round Rock Health Clinic (2120 N. Mays St. Ste 430); Texas A&M Health Science Center (3950 N. A.W. Grimes Blvd., Round Rock); Lake Aire Medical Center (2423 Williams Dr., Georgetown); Georgetown Women's Center (1900 Scenic Dr. Ste 3326); Georgetown Dental (2411 Williams Dr. Ste 111); Georgetown ISD Health & Wellness Center (5001 Airport Rd.); Cedar Park Clinic (1401 Medical Pkwy, Bldg B, Ste 311); Hutto Clinic (123 Ed Schmidt Blvd. Ste 140); Taylor Clinic (1301 West 4th St.); Pflugerville Clinic (1501 W Pecan St. Ste 102).

records.name: Round Rock Housing Authority (Section 8 and Public Housing)
records.description_en: Offers Housing Choice Vouchers (Section 8) and public housing apartments to lower-income families in the Round Rock area.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income families and people in the greater Round Rock area who meet HUD income rules.
records.how_to_apply: Check the website or call to see if waitlists are open, then request an application.
records.notes: Site posted an announcement about opening the Section 8 HCV waitlist (dated March 18, year not confirmed); waitlist status may have changed. Serves about 350 families.

records.name: Georgetown Housing Authority
records.description_en: Runs affordable public housing apartments and the Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher program in Georgetown.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low- and moderate-income households. Staff check family size, income, credit, criminal, and rental history.
documents_needed: Birth certificates and Social Security cards for all household members (at eligibility appointment)
records.how_to_apply: Visit an apartment office during application hours with your ID and Social Security card, or mail a completed application with copies. Renew your application in writing every three months.
records.hours: In-person applications: 11th through end of each month, 9:00am-12:00pm and 1:00pm-4:00pm
records.notes: Currently accepting applications only for Stonehaven Apartments and Shady Oaks Apartments. Section 8 waitlist is CLOSED until further notice. Average wait 9-12 months. Phone (512) 869-6918 is listed for the Section 8 program.

records.name: Taylor Housing Authority (Section 8)
records.description_en: Runs the Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher program that helps low-income families in Taylor pay rent.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income families who meet HUD rules. The waitlist is currently closed.
records.how_to_apply: Watch the website for announcements when the Section 8 waitlist reopens.
records.notes: As of December 23, 2025, THA no longer offers public housing. Waitlist closed; opens only every few years. Second phone: (512) 365-5464.

records.name: Home Repair Program and Homeownership
records.organization: Habitat for Humanity of Williamson County
records.description_en: Helps qualified homeowners with critical repairs for health, safety, or weatherization, and helps families buy an affordable home.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For qualified Williamson County homeowners and families. Call to learn the rules.
records.how_to_apply: Call Habitat for Humanity of Williamson County to ask about applying.
records.notes: Home repair program also listed on the City of Georgetown utility assistance page.

records.name: Georgetown Utility Low Income Discount and Penalty Waivers
records.organization: City of Georgetown - Georgetown Utility Systems
records.description_en: Gives Georgetown utility customers on Medicaid discounts on water, electric, and wastewater bills. Seniors and disabled customers can get late penalty waivers.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Discount: a permanent household member takes part in Medicaid. Penalty waiver: customers 60 or older or with a disability.
documents_needed: Social Security Administration award letter (penalty waiver)
records.how_to_apply: Log in to your CSS portal account and submit the request under Requests.
records.notes: Discounts: 30% water base rate, 30% electric base rate, 20% wastewater rate.

records.name: The Good Neighbor Fund
records.organization: City of Georgetown / The Caring Place
records.description_en: Helps Georgetown utility customers who are having trouble paying their utility bills.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For Georgetown Utility Systems customers having a hard time paying their bills.
records.how_to_apply: Contact The Caring Place, which runs the fund.

records.name: PEC Member Assistance Program (Williamson County)
records.organization: Pedernales Electric Cooperative (distributed by OWBC in Williamson County)
records.description_en: Gives up to $300 a year toward electric bills for Pedernales Electric Cooperative members who qualify.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For PEC members whose name is on the account. Accounts with meter tampering are not eligible.
records.how_to_apply: In Williamson County, contact Opportunities for Williamson & Burnet Counties (OWBC). Applying does not guarantee help.
records.notes: Only for PEC electric customers (parts of Cedar Park, Leander, Liberty Hill, etc.). Limit $300 per year for current usage.

records.name: Utility Bill Assistance (Williamson County)
records.description_en: Helps Williamson County residents who have trouble paying utility bills. Help is given by phone and email.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For Williamson County residents having difficulty paying utility bills.
records.how_to_apply: Call Catholic Charities of Central Texas; help is provided remotely by phone and email.
records.notes: Confirmed via City of Georgetown's assistance list, not Catholic Charities' own site.

records.name: Salvation Army Food and Rent/Utility Help
records.description_en: Offers food help and help paying rent and utility bills.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in need in the Georgetown area. Call to learn the rules.
records.how_to_apply: Call the Salvation Army.
records.notes: Listed on City of Georgetown's utility assistance page; exact service area and office location not confirmed.

records.name: Society of St. Vincent de Paul Emergency Assistance
records.organization: The Society of St. Vincent de Paul
records.description_en: Gives emergency money help to people and families going through hard times.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For individuals and families facing financial hardship.
records.how_to_apply: Call and leave a message; someone will call you back.
records.notes: Listed on City of Georgetown's utility assistance page; service area not confirmed.

records.name: Round Rock Rides (On-Demand Transit)
records.description_en: Low-cost shared rides you can book by app, website, or phone to get around Round Rock. Wheelchair-accessible vehicles are available.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to the public in Round Rock. Reduced $2 fare for seniors 65+ with ID, paratransit-eligible riders, and active-duty military.
records.how_to_apply: Book a ride with the Round Rock Rides app, at book.roundrock.rideco.com, or by phone.
records.hours: Mon-Fri 6:00am-8:00pm; Sat 8:00am-6:00pm; closed Sunday and major holidays. Phone booking Mon-Fri 6:30am-7:30pm, Sat 8:30am-5:30pm.

records.name: Round Rock ADA Paratransit
records.description_en: Shared, curb-to-curb rides for people with disabilities in Round Rock.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people with disabilities who complete an application and an in-person interview.
records.how_to_apply: Fill out the ADA application from the city's transit page and complete an in-person interview.
records.cost: $2.00 per boarding; personal care attendants ride free
records.notes: Phone shown is the Round Rock Rides booking line on the same transit page; confirm the paratransit-specific number.

records.name: GoGeo Paratransit
records.description_en: Curb-to-curb rides for people with disabilities who live in Georgetown city limits.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For qualified people with disabilities living inside Georgetown city limits.
records.how_to_apply: Book at least 24 hours ahead by calling 512-478-RIDE (7433).
records.notes: City transit office: transit@georgetowntexas.gov, 300-1 Industrial Ave, Georgetown. Page also mentions rideGTX (Uber/zTrip voucher partnership) and Faith in Action Georgetown volunteer rides for seniors 65+.

records.name: CARTS Country Bus - Williamson County
records.description_en: Curb-to-curb van rides by reservation for people in rural Williamson County, including trips to nearby towns and connections to buses to Austin.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to the public in rural parts of Williamson County. Half fare for adults 65+, people with disabilities, and children 12 and under with an adult.
records.how_to_apply: Call CARTS at least 24 hours before you need the ride.
records.notes: All CARTS buses and vans are wheelchair accessible. Interurban 1514 Silver Route Taylor-Austin $4 one way. CARTS administrative phone: (512) 481-1011.

records.name: CARTS NOW Taylor (On-Demand Rides)
records.description_en: On-demand rides anywhere in Taylor city limits, usually within 15 minutes, booked with an app.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to anyone traveling within Taylor city limits.
records.how_to_apply: Download the CARTS NOW app and request a ride.
records.notes: Fare ($2) confirmed on ridecarts.com Williamson page; hours on City of Taylor page.

records.name: Free Civil Legal Services
records.description_en: Free legal help for low-income people with civil problems like housing, eviction, benefits, and family issues.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income people in TRLA's service counties, including Williamson County.
records.how_to_apply: Call the toll-free intake line on weekdays to apply.
records.notes: Austin office serves Williamson County residents. Local intake line: (956) 996-8752.
